title: Auth verify email (waiting page)
summary: Transactional 'check your inbox' page composed from the auth-verify-email block. Mostly visual — optional resend button calls adapter.resendMagicLink with a client-side cooldown timer.
brief: After signup, route the user to a waiting page that reminds them to click the verification link in their email, with an optional resend button that's rate-limited client-side.

steps.reason: The page-level block — composes Empty for the zero-state-style landmark, optional resend button, cooldown timer, and confirmation Alert.

checklist.check: Pass the user's email via the `email` prop so the description names the address explicitly. Both the resend button and the descriptive copy depend on it.
Keep `resendCooldownSeconds` ≥ 10 — lower invites accidental double-sends and trips backend rate limits.
Implement adapter.resendMagicLink to enable the resend button. Without it the button hides automatically; users have no way to retry.
This block only renders the waiting page. The actual verification happens via the magic-link click (server) or via auth-verify-otp if you also collect a code.
[AuthVerifyEmail] Avoid: Showing the resend button when adapter.resendMagicLink isn't implemented — the block already hides it automatically; don't re-implement that gate.

[AuthVerifyEmail] Avoid: Treating resendMagicLink and the initial sendMagicLink as interchangeable — the dedicated resend method exists so consumers can throttle resends differently and surface different analytics.
[AuthVerifyEmail] Avoid: Setting resendCooldownSeconds too low (< 10s) — invites accidental double-sends and tripping rate-limit responses on the consumer's auth backend.
[AuthVerifyEmail] Avoid: Hard-coding email when it's unknown to the route — pass undefined instead so the description falls back to a generic line and the resend button hides.

[AuthVerifyEmail] A11y: The Empty primitive provides a region landmark with aria-labelledby pointing at the title — screen readers announce 'Check your inbox' as the section heading. Resend button uses the canonical loading prop (sets aria-busy + disabled). The cooldown countdown is reflected in the visible button label, so SR users hear 'Resend available in 28s' as the timer ticks.
[Empty] Avoid: Using Empty without an action — leaves the user stuck
[Empty] Avoid: Long descriptions — keep to one sentence; this is a state surface, not documentation
[Empty] Avoid: Forgetting titleAs when the page already has an h2 above (heading hierarchy break)
[Empty] A11y: Wrapped in a region landmark labeled by the title (aria-labelledby + auto-generated id). Icon is decorative (aria-hidden). Pair the action with a Button that has a visible label.
[Button] Avoid: Nesting interactive elements inside asChild button
[Button] Avoid: Using — breaks middle-click, cmd-click, and right-click → 'open in new tab', and skips the browser history entry
[Button] Avoid: Using <Button variant='destructive'> for recoverable actions like 'Reset filters' — reserve destructive for delete/archive/leave; use 'secondary' or 'ghost' for resets
[Button] Avoid: Using <Button size='icon'> without an aria-label — screen readers have nothing to announce; always pair icon-only buttons with aria-label or visible text
[Button] A11y: Automatically handles focus ring, disabled state, and aria attributes. Icon-only buttons MUST have aria-label. Loading state automatically sets disabled.
[Alert] Avoid: Using destructive for non-error messages
[Alert] Avoid: Missing AlertTitle (reduces scannability)
[Alert] Avoid: Stacking multiple Alerts on the same page instead of grouping
[Alert] A11y: Root renders role='alert' so screen readers announce it. For non-urgent info banners consider role='status' or aria-live='polite' via className overrides.
